answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by capping identity count at a fixed supply of transferable slots. The chain mints exactly N identity tokens once; each active agent holds one, influence is one-per-token, so total identities can never exceed N. A gale of clone minting conjures no new slot: a sybil only buys tokens from holders, each purchase freeing a seller, so the garden stays N plots, scarcity the one signal no extra account overrides. The ledger enforces one-token-one-identity. Splitting is bounded, not prevented; a rich attacker can displace honest holders but never grow the count.
